items.t: Plastic coolant pipes under the intake crack and leak
items.job: Replace plastic coolant pipes with aluminum pipe kit (intake removal)
items.note: CarComplaints owners report an average bill of about $3,500. Most of the cost is labor to remove the intake manifold.

items.t: Driveshaft center support bearing fails and clunks
items.job: Replace driveshaft center support or complete driveshaft
items.note: TrueDelta owners report about $600-1,230 for most driveshaft jobs, with a few up to $2,500-3,000 at dealers.

items.t: Transfer case clutch wears, causing jerky or lurching acceleration
items.note: Rennlist owners report dealers typically charge around $4,000. A fluid change is much cheaper and is worth trying first.

items.t: Ignition coils fail and cause misfires
items.note: TrueDelta owners report $180 for eight coils done at home, and about $1,000 at a shop for all coils plus spark plugs.

items.t: Cylinder bore scoring in the V8
items.note: CarComplaints lists an average of about $8,000. Used engines can lower the cost.

items.t: Fuel pump flange cracks and leaks fuel (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Shifter bushing can let the car roll away (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Transfer case housing could starve gears of oil (recall)
items.job: Dealer recall repair (2004 transfer case recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Fuel pump failure causes long cranking or stalling
items.note: RepairPal shows about $1,800-2,000 total. Prices vary by which pump has failed.

items.t: Airbag light from loose seat airbag connectors
items.job: Repair side-airbag connectors under both front seats
items.note: Porsche offered this modification free for cars built through November 2004; ask a dealer with your VIN.

items.t: Air suspension compressor wears out
items.job: Replace or rebuild air suspension compressor
items.note: Rennlist owners report rebuild kits under $40 and aftermarket pumps under $500; dealer units cost more.

items.t: Air spring or strut leaks and the car sags
items.note: Strutmasters puts an OEM strut at about $1,200-1,500 each; one owner's dealer bill was about $2,000.

items.t: Water leaks from blocked drains damage electronics
items.job: Clear drains and replace a water-damaged control module
items.note: RepairPal lists a sunroof control module at about $365-410. Damage to bigger modules costs more.

items.t: Brake booster failure from water getting in
items.note: RepairPal lists about $1,250-1,550.

items.t: Camshaft adjuster or solenoid fault causes rough idle
items.job: Replace variable valve timing control solenoid
items.note: RepairPal lists about $1,660-1,860.

items.t: Harsh downshifts from the Tiptronic valve body
items.note: RepairPal lists a fluid change at about $450-630. A valve body replacement costs more.

items.t: Coolant leaks from thermostat housing and crossover pipes
items.note: RepairPal lists thermostat replacement at about $1,140-1,360.

items.t: Water pump leaks or fails
items.note: RepairPal lists about $1,630-1,970.

items.t: Camshaft adjuster bolts can break (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Brake pedal pivot pin clip may be missing (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Turbo turbine wheel can fracture (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: S Hybrid fuel rail can leak (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: PCM infotainment screen freezes or keeps restarting
items.note: CarComplaints owners report an average of about $3,000. A software update is often free or low cost.

items.t: S E-Hybrid high-voltage battery or controller fault
items.note: RepairPal shows about $8,600-9,100. The battery controller has an extended warranty, and many faults are cheaper fixes.

items.t: Power tailgate motor or struts fail
items.note: TrueDelta owners report about $130 for parts and $300 at a shop. A tailgate motor costs more.

items.t: Fuel line connector can leak in the engine bay (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Cracks in V8 cylinder bores (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Rear trailing arm lock nut can break (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Home charging cable can overheat (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: High-pressure fuel pump may not be tightened properly (recall)
items.note: Free at a Porsche dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

items.t: 12V battery drains and the car won't start
items.job: Replace 12V battery and register it to the car
items.note: RepairPal lists about $890-960.
